I graduated college last semester and I've currently been searching for a job for the last two weeks. The only information I have to go off of is from sites like headhunter or indeed.com, and I have received no responses from the 20+ jobs I've applied for on these sites, which makes me think these sites aren't the best place to be looking.

I heard this one employer in my city was hiring, and I went to their website and there are indeed many openings there. This company was in my own city, and it took me two weeks to accidentally come across this information. Is there a way to speed up this process or discover more jobs in my field?
Is there a method of finding jobs/careers in my field and which companies are hiring for them?

Look up the companies themselves and go to their websites. Think of where you want to work and look up a rankings list of best employers or just biggest employers, and sift through it and check the website for the companies that seem like they might have a position for whatever field you're in.

If a job is posted to a site like indeed then they might be inundated with applications. If it's just on their website and maybe one or two other places they'll have less of a pile to get through. A lot of the time they dont want "the best" they want clay that they can teach how to do things the way they want them done, so it doesnt add value for them to sift through all those extra applications.

Also, it's better to apply through the corporate website and with a cover letter showing that you know something about thier company and why you are interested.

Sites like Indeed are good for finding out the places easily and applying en-masse. It's nice but don't seriously expect any of them to reply to you - it's made for sending out like 50 applications a week and seeing what bites. I have gotten several jobs through Indeed, it's often just a huge amount of applications and giving them a bit of time.

In many fields it's becoming less what you know and more of who you know - try making connections with someone who already works in the field that you want to get into and try and get a reference through them.
And in some areas, where you went to school.

Drive/walk/bike around business districts/sections and write down names on signs and buildings. Then visit their websites and see what they have. I've gotten a job through a reference via my wife, Dice, Zip Recruiter and a direct website application. If you are new to the workforce, go to temp agencies like Apple One, they might have something in your field or not (but an office job will look good depending on how you can spin it), but you'll have to be an extremely squeaky wheel if they don't have any positions in your field.
